lines.say: In an exponential, x is the power. Here the base is 2.
Make a table. Each step right doubles y.
Plot the points and join them with a smooth curve.
Every one of these graphs passes through 0, 1, because a to the power 0 is 1.
Going left, the curve gets closer and closer to the x-axis.
It never touches it. The x-axis is an asymptote.
Now add y equals 3 to the x. A bigger base rises more steeply.
If a is greater than 1, the graph rises. That's exponential growth.
A base between 0 and 1, like a half, makes the graph fall.
That's exponential decay. A half to the x is a mirror image of 2 to the x.
All of them pass through 0, 1 and stay above the x-axis.
lines.alt: y = 2ˣ, y = 3ˣ and y = (½)ˣ all pass through (0, 1)

lines.say: Work out 3 to the x for x from minus 2 to 2.
Plot the five points.
Join them smoothly. Each step right multiplies y by 3.
On the left, the curve hugs the x-axis but never reaches it.
Multiply by k, and the y-intercept moves to 0, k.
Example. Five times 3 to the x starts at 5, not 1.
The asymptote stays at y equals 0.
If k is negative, the graph flips below the x-axis.
Do the power first. At x equals 2, three times 2 to the x is 12.
Adding c moves every point up. Subtracting moves it down.
The asymptote moves too. Here it drops to y equals minus 3.
The y-intercept is 1 minus 3, which is minus 2.
Now the curve crosses the x-axis, at about 1.58.
Draw the curve rising to the right, hugging y equals minus 3 on the left.
A graph y equals k times a to the x goes through 0, 5 and 2, 45.
The y-intercept gives k. So k is 5.
Use the other point. 45 equals 5 times a squared.
So a squared is 9, and a is 3. It must be positive.
The rule is y equals 5 times 3 to the x.
y equals a to the x never crosses the x-axis. Only shifted graphs can.
The y-intercept is only 0, 1 for the basic graph.
Don't mix up 2 to the x with x squared. In 2 to the x, x is the power.
Remember to move the asymptote. Two to the x plus 5 has asymptote y equals 5.
Every basic exponential says hello at 0, 1.
Base bigger than 1 grows. Base between 0 and 1 decays.
The number added on is the asymptote.
